steps.title: Open the dashboard
steps.narration: Trendora opens on a market command center — a chart that already reaches back three decades, with every benchmark line honestly labeled by where its data comes from.
steps.point_out: Look at the far-left edge of the chart: the deep index and volatility lines run all the way back to 1996, while the newer ETF lines start later — exactly as expected.

steps.title: Follow the market regime to its evidence
steps.narration: The dashboard reads today's market regime and links straight to the track record behind it, so no score sits unexplained.
steps.point_out: This ledger entry shows exactly how a Risk-on-regime idea performed out of sample — and it's honest about the loss.

target.name: See evidence proven in this regime →

expect.text: Out-of-sample edge in the Risk-on regime

steps.title: Audit the evidence ledger
steps.narration: Every past trading idea on this ledger is graded against real, out-of-sample results — right now every single one honestly reads FAIL, nothing dressed up.
steps.point_out: Each row links back to exactly where it would apply — click through and you land on the real stock list it was tested against.

steps.title: Browse and sort the stock list
steps.narration: All 541 currently tracked companies are right here, and every score is honestly marked not-yet-proven until real evidence backs it.
steps.point_out: Try sorting by sector — the table reorders instantly, with nothing lost or hidden in the shuffle.

steps.title: Drill into a single stock
steps.narration: Every ticker — like NVIDIA here — gets its own page carrying the same no-hype scoring shown on the full list.
steps.point_out: Leadership, Entry Quality, and Risk are all marked "Not yet proven" — the honesty rule follows the stock everywhere.

steps.title: See three decades of history in one click
steps.narration: A single toggle swaps the chart from a recent window to the stock's entire trading history.
steps.point_out: The caption now reports thousands of bars, with older history clearly and honestly marked as weekly-sampled.

steps.title: Check where the chart's data comes from
steps.narration: The Data Manager page discloses exactly which vendor supplied every index and macro line on that dashboard chart, and how far back its history genuinely goes.
steps.point_out: Even an economic-indicator proxy is labeled honestly by its real source — never a fabricated figure.

steps.title: Read the data coverage calendar
steps.narration: The same page's coverage calendar makes two things visually obvious at once: which days simply have price data, and which days also have a fully scored snapshot.
steps.point_out: A violet ring marks a scored day; the legend spells out exactly what each color and ring mean.

steps.title: One consistent company count everywhere
steps.narration: The number of actively tracked companies always matches, whether you're looking at the stock list or the data manager's own count.
steps.point_out: 541 companies today, counted the same way on both pages.
